{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUhJrVs8AAAABS5_bpA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bkfq-zg8ewfw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bkfq-", "number": 8, "title": "Add development and review guidelines", "body": "## Problem

three-webmcp has no documented contribution or review conventions. Apart from the README's "Development and validation" section and CI, the repository has:

- no Issue template
- no Pull Request template
- no documented development flow
- no review guidelines

This matters more now that work may be implemented by AI agents (for example through ProjectWeave/GitWeave): the Issue text becomes the task description, and there is no shared reference for what a complete, appropriately scoped change and its review look like.

## Expected outcome

Add lightweight development and review conventions following the same approach as GitWeave and ProjectWeave:

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md` — Problem / Expected outcome / Context
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — Summary / Outcome / Validation / Related issues
- `docs/development-flow.md` — Issue → Pull Request → Review → Revision if needed → Merge
- `docs/review-guidelines.md` — review against the Issue: no missing work, no unnecessary work, then ordinary quality checks

The content should match the GitWeave/ProjectWeave versions, with project names adapted to three-webmcp. Where validation is mentioned, it may refer to the existing checks (`npm test`, `npm run example:build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm pack`) that the README and CI already define; do not introduce new checks.

## Context

References (identical in both repositories):

- https://github.com/takahirox/projectweave/tree/main/.github
- https://github.com/takahirox/projectweave/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md
- https://github.com/takahirox/projectweave/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md
- ProjectWeave added all four files in one change: https://github.com/takahirox/projectweave/pull/3

Out of scope:

- `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` or other files the reference repositories do not have
- the project license (tracked in #7)
- branch protection, rulesets or other repository settings
- changes to code, tests or CI
